org.name: Butterfly Rescue Ranch
org.tagline: Every horse has a story; every loving heart deserves to see it.

horses.title: Rico
horses.alt: Rico, a white horse in a red halter, looks into the camera beside a red pipe gate
horses.lede: Pulled from a kill pen, brought back to health, sent to a home that failed him, and brought back again. He stays at the ranch for good now. In Braxton's words, he is “a genuine saint of a horse.”
quote: He's just a sweet old boy that we use for lessons now. He's great with kids.
log: Braxton bought Rico out of the kill pen in Stillwater, where horses wait to be shipped to Mexico for slaughter.
Feed, hay, supplements and the farrier, every day and every six weeks, until he was sound and at weight.
About $360 a month in set costs, before the vet
The ranch found Rico a home.
That home failed him. He came back to the ranch in worse condition than the first time.
Braxton thinks he was once a reining horse. Now he carries young riders a couple of times a week and spends the rest of it retired. He stays at the ranch for the rest of his life.

horses.title: Reba
horses.alt: Reba, a chestnut mare with a white blaze and a green rope halter, under a blue sky
horses.lede: Reba came from auction with an old injury to her right knee that nobody could explain. The knee will probably always be a little swollen, but she moves better every month, and her slow, gentle way makes her the horse new riders start on. Braxton plans to find her a home in time.
quote: Because of her sweet spirit, she's been able to be used for lessons for beginner riders.
log: Her right knee was already swollen when the ranch picked her up. Auction horses come with no papers and no history.
An auction horse gets the vet, the farrier and a dental check first. Feet and teeth hide a lot of problems.
Gentle lead-line work, because moving is better for the joint than standing still. She gets around much better than when she arrived.
The horse new riders start on
She takes things slow and is gentle with kids, so beginners ride Reba and Rico first.
About $360 a month in set costs

horses.title: Dandelion
horses.alt: Dandelion, a buckskin mare in a pink rope halter, looking into the camera
horses.lede: Dandelion was in the Stillwater kill pen, headed for slaughter in Mexico, when Braxton bought her. She was so skittish the staff could tell someone had hurt her. Given time to learn that nobody here would, she came round, and now she carries the more advanced kids in lessons. Braxton plans to find her a home in time.
quote: Once she had a little bit of love and a little bit of time to realize that nobody was going to hurt her anymore, she was able to be put into the riding lessons.
card: A little ditzy, in the best way
log: Bought out of the kill pen
Headed for Mexico for slaughter, with no history at all and scared of everyone.
Months of patience before she trusted people again.
About $360 a month in set costs
Lessons, and running in the field

She carries the more confident kids in lessons. In the field she runs around without watching where she's going, which is how she got the small cut on her neck. It's sprayed with a liquid bandage to keep it clean.

horses.title: Daisy
horses.alt: Daisy, a cream mare with a pale mane in a red halter, by the red pipe gate
horses.lede: Daisy came from the same Stillwater kill pen with no history at all, except that she was a skeleton when the ranch picked her up and frightened of everyone. Right now her only job is putting weight on and getting strong. When she's healthy, Braxton will find her a loving home.
quote: She was a skeleton when they picked her up. She's a pretty big mystery, honestly.
log: No papers, no history, and scared of people. Someone at the sale said she'd been ridden bareback; the staff take that with a grain of salt.
Feed and hay every day to put weight back on. She isn't being ridden yet.
$9 a day in hay and feed
Once she's healthy, the staff will see what she's like under saddle and Braxton will find her the right home.

people.name: Braxton Brackin
people.alt: Braxton Brackin in a pink western shirt and straw hat, holding a buckskin horse at a rodeo arena
people.bio: Raised around rodeo and riding for 27 years, Braxton learned calf roping from her uncle before she could walk. She still competes, and teaches with a firm but encouraging style that helps students believe they can do anything they set their minds to.

people.name: Anna Foote
people.alt: Anna Foote cheek to cheek with a dark horse with a white blaze, mountains behind
people.bio: Born and raised in Cody, Wyoming, Anna rode six years with a rodeo drill team before moving to Oklahoma after college in 2023. She loves breakaway roping and teaching riders of every age, and making it fun.

people.name: Chloe Bjornberg
people.alt: Chloe Bjornberg in a navy show jacket, standing with a dapple grey horse
people.bio: A former president of the OU Equestrian Team, Chloe has taught English and western lessons for over eight years. She's now in graduate school at OU, working toward becoming a counselor who offers equine-assisted therapy.

how._comment: The 'How it works' switch (header). Each note names the Station product behind a feature and says what it does ON THE LIVE SITE. Only the email sign-ups are connected on this preview (to Station Give, the ranch's list; no email is sent until the ranch's mailbox is connected), so no note may claim a feature works now, or anything the products do not do. No invented prices or numbers. Features carry data-how=<key> in build.py; 'spots' are matched by selector for parts other scripts build. Rendered by _src/how.js.
how.legend: Each outlined part of this page is run by a Station product, named in the note beside it. This site is a preview. Email sign-ups already go to the ranch’s own list; donations, the chat and texts switch on when the site goes live. The notes say what happens then.

herd: Every horse gets its own page, following it from the day it arrived to the day it is well.
The same story goes out as the ranch’s two-a-week horse series on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
journal: Each step of the horse’s recovery, and what it cost, is added to this page as it happens.
The same updates go out as the two-a-week horse series on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
The monthly email tells donors which horses moved forward and what their gifts paid for.
news: Each post here also goes out on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
Once a month the news goes to everyone on the ranch’s email list.
join: The address joins the ranch’s own email list. Once a month, everyone on it hears how the horses are doing.
giver: Secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account: card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank. The money goes straight to the ranch, and a tax receipt arrives by email at once.
Monthly donors update their card or stop their gift from the link in their receipt. A card that fails is retried automatically.
promise: Every donor gets a thank-you from Braxton within the hour. A gift of $250 or more also alerts Braxton to call the donor personally.
Donors get the horse updates, a summary of their giving each January, and the Giving Tuesday appeal.
A donor who has not given for 12 months gets a short note from the ranch inviting them back.
levels: A sponsorship is a monthly gift through secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account, with a tax receipt by email. Sponsors update their card or stop it from their receipt link, and a failed card is retried automatically.
Each new sponsor gets a thank-you from Braxton within the hour.
The monthly note on the horse, the January giving summary and Giving Tuesday all go out by email.
logos: Radar finds local businesses that fit, like feed and tack stores, vet clinics and riding programs, and lines them up in the ranch’s sponsor pipeline for the ask.
A business sponsors through the same secure monthly checkout, with a receipt for every payment.
volunteer: Every sign-up gets a welcome by text and email the same day, and follow-ups until the volunteer replies.
The welcome links to the ranch’s booking page, where a new volunteer picks a first barn day and gets a reminder before it.
flyer: Families pick a lesson, camp or pony party and book it themselves, and reminders by text and email make sure they turn up.
where: The ranch’s Google listing is kept to one name, one address and one set of hours, with the donate and volunteer links and a horse update each week.
After a visit or a volunteer day, everyone who came is asked for a Google review, not only the happy ones. Braxton approves a drafted reply to each review.
call: When nobody can get to the phone, a missed call gets a text back within seconds.
An AI receptionist answers the ranch’s number, takes a message on surrender and welfare calls, and passes urgent ones straight to Braxton.
facts: Built by Station on the ranch’s own photos and words, and the ranch’s to keep.
The same name, address and phone are kept on the ranch’s Google listing, so the two never disagree.
links: Every social bio points here instead of Linktree, so a follower is one tap from Donate.
“Get the monthly update” turns a follower into someone on the ranch’s own email list.
greet: An AI assistant answers from the ranch’s own facts at any hour, and takes the visitor’s details so the ranch can follow up.
footer: The sign-up on the magenta sheet below joins the same monthly email list.
The ranch’s number gets missed-call text-back and the AI receptionist.
“donate.” goes to the same secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account.
